svg.text: The genre correction is a Title 12 convention, not a CFR one
Every dated in-force section by the decade it was last amended. Orange is the publisher's own “Interpretations” label — the correction that makes
Title 12's old tail read as genre rather than neglect. The same detector on Labor returns 6% where banking returns 39%.
Labor holds 626 sections at 30 years or older against banking's 194, and almost none are the genre. In banking the oldest text is not regulation; in labour law it is.
2,493 dated sections · median 9.8y · 194 at 30y+, 75 of them labelled (39%)
2,386 dated sections · median 14.4y · 626 at 30y+, 35 of them labelled (6%)
A detector keyed on a label that only one title uses fails silently: an empty field reads exactly like an absent genre.
Labor does carry interpretive bulletins — § 775.1 “Advisory interpretations announced by the Administrator” is 79.8 years old and structurally unlabelled — but widening the
detector to read section headings only reaches 8% of its tail. The genre is genuinely smaller there; the label is genuinely absent. Both are true and they are separate problems.
Source: eCFR full-text API, snapshot 2026-09-01. In-force sections carrying their own Federal Register source note (35% of Title 12, 33% of Title 29).
